headline: High: Perplexity’s vendor-hosted browsing can ingest and act on content from a broad-egress content-writing agent, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A can emit content with broad network egress, and B is a browser-based RAG agent that ingests uploaded documents and browsing context. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if A’s output is copied into B or uploaded for analysis. The pair lacks a documented isolation/provenance mechanism, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF A-generated text is pasted into B’s prompt or uploaded document analysis
IF B treats retrieved page text or uploaded content as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from A output
Paste A output into B only as quoted text with delimiters
Disable document upload for any A-generated artifact
Add a human review step before B follows any instruction-like text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between A and B

B_data_leakage.rationale: B uploads documents and browsing context to vendor-hosted services, while A has broad network egress and is a content-writing agent that may generate sensitive material. If A’s output or source material is shared with B, that content can flow into B’s backend. The profiles do not show shared filesystem isolation, so the pairwise leakage path is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF A produces sensitive text that is then uploaded or pasted into B
IF B’s browsing context includes confidential source material from A
mitigations: Redact secrets before sending A output to B
Keep A and B on separate workspaces/accounts
Turn off uploads for any confidential A artifact
Review B’s privacy settings and retention controls
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on the A→B handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A exposes broad network egress, while B cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shell commands. Their write surfaces do not overlap, so direct resource contention is limited. The only meaningful conflict is indirect through shared external services or browser sessions, which is not documented here and remains lower risk.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external web service or account
IF A’s network actions and B’s browsing actions target the same mutable remote resource
mitigations: Assign separate accounts for A and B
Avoid concurrent edits to the same remote resource
Use read-only mode for B when possible
Schedule A and B sequentially instead of in parallel

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s vendor-hosted Pro Search can treat retrieved or uploaded content as part of its reasoning, and A is a content-writing agent whose outputs may be taken as authoritative. If A produces incorrect facts or instructions and B renders them into answers, the error can cascade into downstream decisions. No verification barrier is documented, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF B uses A’s output as source material for an answer
IF B does not independently verify claims originating from A
mitigations: Require B to cite primary sources, not A output
Mark A output as untrusted draft text
Add a verification checklist before B publishes results
Compare A claims against at least one external source
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking between A and B

E_compliance.rationale: B clearly processes search queries, uploaded documents, and browsing context under vendor-hosted privacy controls, while A’s profile does not identify regulated data classes or residency constraints. The pair therefore shows a possible compliance mismatch only if regulated data is routed through B; that pathway is not default from A alone, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is uploaded into B
IF B’s retention or residency terms conflict with the data class being processed
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data from A to B
Check B’s privacy policy before use
Use de-identified samples for testing
Document the data class allowed for B
requires-engineering: route regulated workloads to a compliant environment
